descriptions.description: An $n$-tuple of positive integers is $G$-harmonic if there are subgroups of $G$ having those indices whose cosets can be chosen pairwise disjoint, and $\mathbb{Z}$-harmonic if there are pairwise disjoint residue classes with those moduli. Ginosar asked whether every $G$-harmonic tuple is $\mathbb{Z}$-harmonic. Margolis and Schnabel proved this for tuples of length at most $4$, and analysed a particular family of length-$5$ tuples that would yield a counterexample if any member were $G$-harmonic. We show that the bound $4$ is sharp: $(6,6,6,10,15)$ is $A_5$-harmonic but not $\mathbb{Z}$-harmonic. Moreover, the five pairwise disjoint cosets realising this tuple can be extended to a coset partition of $A_5$ using only cosets of indices $6$, $10$, and $15$. The index tuple of this partition is not $\mathbb{Z}$-harmonic; because its indices repeat, this does not contradict the Herzog--Schönheim conjecture. We also prove that no member of the length-$5$ family analysed by Margolis and Schnabel in connection with possible counterexamples is $G$-harmonic for any group $G$.

titles.title: SDRIS: The Thermodynamic Horizon beyond N=30 - The Deep Bulk and the Vacuum Boundary (N=31-408)

rightsList.rights: Creative Commons Attribution Share Alike 4.0 International

descriptions.description:
Description / Abstract:

Current cosmological models face significant challenges in explaining the nature of Dark Matter and the apparent fine-tuning of the universe's energy density. Following the establishment of the "Geometric Syntax" and the "Fractal Filter", this final paper in the trilogy, "The Thermodynamic Horizon", defines the boundary conditions of the vacuum lattice within the SDRIS Theory.

We introduce the concept of the Deep Bulk (Layers $31 \le N \le 408$), identifying this region not as empty space, but as a high-capacity thermodynamic sink responsible for the phenomenon of Dark Matter. We propose the Divisor Friction Mechanism as the primary spectral filter of reality:





Prime-numbered layers ($N_p$): Act as lossless reflectors, generating standing waves (visible matter).




Composite layers ($N_c$): Act as absorbers, dissipating energy into internal rotational modes (storage/Dark Matter).



Finally, we derive the mathematical necessity of a finite universe bounded at N=408. We demonstrate that $N=408$ represents the maximum entropic saturation point of the lattice ($3 \times 136$). The subsequent integer, $N=409$, is a Prime Number. Accessing Layer 409 would trigger a transition from total absorption to total reflection—a thermodynamic singularity implying that the universe is a self-limiting computation, capped at the stability limit to prevent a runaway energy cascade.

Supplementary Data:

This upload is supplemented by the SDRIS Bulk Computational Suite (Python/Jupyter), which reproduces the topological friction analysis, the signal transmission simulation, and the 3D Lissajous-Trajectories presented in the paper.

The dataset contains the SDRIS Bulk Computational Suite, a unified Jupyter Notebook used to validate the topological derivations presented in the paper "SDRIS: The Thermodynamic Horizon beyond N=30".

The suite performs numerical analysis and visualizations for the following modules:





Bulk Structure Analysis: Algorithms to map the distribution of 69 Prime Singularities within the vacuum bulk ($31 \le N \le 408$).




Signal Transmission Simulation: A stochastic model demonstrating the "Quantization Filter" effect (analogous to Hawking Radiation) where prime layers distill chaotic noise into harmonic constants.




Tuple-Harmonics Topology: A 3D-visualization engine generating Lissajous trajectories for Dark Matter (Dissonant Tuples) vs. Higgs Boson (Harmonic Tuples).




Friction Analysis: Calculation of the divisor density function $\sigma_0(N)$ to mathematical prove the thermodynamic instability at the boundary $N=409$.



Technical Requirements: Python 3.x, NumPy, Matplotlib.

titles.title: On the inverse problem of Moebius geometry on the circle

descriptions.description: Any (boundary continuous) hyperbolic space induces on the boundary at infinity a Moebius structure which reflects most essential asymptotic properties of the space. In this paper, we initiate the study of the inverse problem: describe Moebius structures which are induced by hyperbolic spaces at least in the simplest case of the circle. For a large class of Moebius structures on the circle, we define a canonical "filling" each of them, which serves as a natural candidate for a solution of the inverse problem. This is a 3-dimensional (pseudo)metric space Harm, which consists of harmonic 4-tuples of the respective Moebius structure with a distance determined by zig-zag paths. Our main result is the proof that every line in Harm is a geodesic, i.e., shortest in the zig-zag distance on each segment. This gives a good starting point to show that Harm is Gromov hyperbolic with the prescribed Moebius structure at infinity.
